title: Web App Starter: AWS vs Google Cloud vs Azure
subtitle: Architecture and cost comparison (skill test run)
author: Cloud Cost Comparator
infographic_title: Web App Starter: which cloud fits?
executive_summary: Azure has the lowest monthly list price for this small design, both on demand and with 1 year commitments. The three clouds sit within 9% of each other on demand, so the choice should rest on team skills and services rather than price alone.
Internet egress drives most of the difference: Google Cloud charges more per GB and has no monthly free allowance in this estimate, while AWS and Azure each make the first 100 GB free.
scope: The brief describes two web servers, 500 GB of stored files and about 200 GB of data downloaded by users each month. Databases, load balancing, backups and monitoring are out of scope for this test.
requirements: Run two general purpose web servers continuously
Store 500 GB of frequently read files
Serve about 200 GB per month to users over the internet

aws: Two EC2 m7i.large instances serve the application and read and write files in an S3 Standard bucket. Responses leave AWS as internet data transfer.
gcp: Two Compute Engine n2-standard-2 instances serve the application with files in a regional Cloud Storage Standard bucket. Traffic leaves on the Premium network tier.
azure: Two D2s v5 virtual machines serve the application with files in Blob Storage (Hot, locally redundant). Traffic leaves over the Microsoft network.

variance_discussion: Egress accounts for about 60% of the component level differences. Web servers account for about 31%: Azure's D2s v5 is the cheapest VM on demand and with a 1 year reservation. Google Cloud has the cheapest storage, but at 500 GB that saves only about $1 to $2 a month.

risks: Prices are list prices for a single month and exclude taxes, support plans and negotiated discounts.
Google Cloud was priced in Iowa because the rendered page defaulted to that region; US East prices may differ.
Disks attached to the VMs, load balancing and backups are not included and would add cost on every cloud.
next_steps: Confirm the monthly download volume, since it drives most of the gap.
Price Google Cloud in us-east1 with the Billing Catalog API key.
Add block storage, load balancing and backups before using the totals for budgeting.
